paper_sections.title: Conditional and syllogistic deductive tasks dissociate functionally during premise integration
Neuroimaging Evidence on Encoding and Integration
Functional Homogeneity of the Syllogistic Network
Encoding of Premises During Conditional and Syllogistic Reasoning
Integration of Premises During Conditional and Quantified Reasoning

description.value: The study compared the neural activity associated with conditional and syllogistic deductive reasoning, separately examining premise encoding and premise integration in the same participants.

design.value: A within-participants, event-related fMRI study comparing conditional and syllogistic deductive problems and assessing the encoding and integration stages of deduction. Participants completed reasoning and memory trials during four fMRI runs.

name.value: problem type (syllogisms vs. conditionals) × task (reasoning vs. memory)

source_definition.value: The interaction tested whether the reasoning-related encoding activation differed between syllogistic and conditional premises.

name.value: problem type (syllogisms vs. conditionals) × condition (integrable vs. non-integrable)

source_definition.value: The interaction compared the integration effect for syllogisms with the integration effect for conditionals.

description.value: Twenty-six healthy subjects (aged 25 years on average, SD: 5.0; 15 males) participated in the experiment. All were right-handed, had normal vision, with no neurological or psychiatric history.

acquired_count.value: Twenty-six healthy subjects participated in the experiment

task_description.value: Participants performed conditional and categorical syllogistic deductive reasoning problems and memory trials during event-related fMRI. The reasoning problems required reading premises, drawing a conclusion whenever possible, and recognizing the inferred conclusion from four alternatives. The study separately assessed encoding of the first premise and integration of the second premise.

instructions.value: Subjects were informed they would do either a reasoning or a memory task. In reasoning trials, they were asked to read each premise and, whenever possible, draw a new conclusion promptly and accurately. In memory trials, they were told to read and remember sentences carefully for fast recognition from among four subsequently presented sentences.

stimuli.value: Deductive problems consisted of two or three premises and four alternative conclusions. Sentences described qualities of an unspecified thing using nonexistent two-syllabic adjectives with a plausible phonological structure in Italian. The study included conditional problems, categorical syllogisms, and single-premise memory trials.

task_performance_measures.value: Average accuracy for conditional and main-set syllogistic problems
Heuristic index: proportion of responses that were wrong but consistent with the atmosphere heuristic in the nonheuristic set of syllogistic problems
Reaction times on integrable and non-integrable sentences for both conditional and syllogistic problems

modality.value: Blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) contrast using echo planar T2*-weighted imaging (EPI)

instrument.value: 3T Siemens Allegra head scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Acquisition of 32 transverse slices provided coverage of the whole cerebral cortex. In-plane resolution was 3 mm × 3 mm; slice thickness and gap were 2.5 mm and 1.25 mm, respectively.

number_of_volumes.value: on average 1561 volumes for each subject, ranging from a minimum of 1355 volumes to a maximum of 1748 volumes

description.value: The absence of gross structural brain abnormalities was checked on structural scans.

The first four image volumes of each run were discarded. Preprocessing included rigid-body transformation (realignment) and slice timing to correct for head movement and slice acquisition delays. Images were normalized to MNI space using nonlinear warping implemented in SPM2 and smoothed with an 8 mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian filter. Time series were high-pass filtered at 128 s and prewhitened using an autoregressive model AR(1).

steps.value: Discard the first four image volumes of each run to allow stabilization of longitudinal magnetization
Rigid-body transformation (realignment) to correct for head movement
Slice timing correction for slice acquisition delays
Nonlinear normalization to MNI space using SPM2
Spatial smoothing with a Gaussian filter of 8 mm full-width at half maximum
Prewhitening by means of an autoregressive model AR(1)

model_settings.value: Data were best fitted at every voxel for each participant using the effects of interest. The effects of interest were the times of onset of 18 event types within each of four fMRI runs. Onsets corresponded to the time of appearance on the screen of the specific stimulus type, delayed by 1 s. Events were modeled as miniblocks with duration corresponding to the timing of stimuli shown on screen; error trials were modeled separately from correct trials.

The participant-level encoding contrast images, corresponding to (reasoning > memory) for conditional and syllogistic first premises, underwent a second step comprising an ANOVA that modeled the mean of each effect. Linear compounds compared the effects using between-subject variance.

The participant-level integration contrast images, corresponding to (integrable > nonintegrable) second premises for conditional and syllogistic problems, underwent a second step comprising an ANOVA that modeled the mean of each effect. Linear compounds compared the effects, and correction for nonsphericity accounted for possible differences in error variance across conditions and nonindependent error terms for repeated measures.

Response times on first premises were analyzed with a 2 × 2 ANOVA with factors task (reasoning vs. memory) and type of problem (syllogistic vs. conditional problems). Response times on second premises were analyzed with a 2 × 2 ANOVA with within-subject factors integrability (integrable vs. nonintegrable premises) and type of problem (syllogistic vs. conditional problems).

The average integration effect for syllogistic problems was extracted across all voxels in six regions of interest for every subject. PCA was run on the resulting 26 × 6 matrix, with varimax orthogonal rotation.

estimator.value: principal component extraction with varimax rotation

description.value: A reasoning trial in which participants solved a deductive problem involving a series of premises and selected the valid conclusion.
A memory trial in which participants read and remembered a single sentence for fast recognition from four subsequently presented sentences.
Propositional reasoning problems using logical connectives such as if…then.
Categorical syllogisms using quantified predicative statements such as every X is Y or no X are Y.
The second premise shared an adjectival term with the first premise, allowing generation of a deductive conclusion.

The second premise did not share an adjectival term with the first premise and therefore could not be integrated with it to generate a valid conclusion; in some trials it was followed by a third premise.
